summary: Compares target/reference objects or world-space point inputs and outputs transform, matrix, bearing, distance, inverse-square, and related spatial relationship channels.

key_params.name: compute
key_params.note: Select transform, matrix, or measurement output family

key_params.name: translate
key_params.note: Output displacement from reference to target

key_params.name: quat
key_params.note: Output quaternion from reference to target

key_params.name: bear
key_params.note: Output bearing rotation needed for reference to face target

key_params.name: xord
key_params.note: Transform order for rotation, scale, transform, and bearing modes

key_params.name: rord
key_params.note: Rotate order for rotation, scale, transform, and bearing modes

key_params.name: appendattribs
key_params.note: Add rotate attributes to generated rotation channels

key_params.name: smoothrotate
key_params.note: Output smooth rotation curves without graphical jumps

key_params.name: outputrange
key_params.note: Current frame, current time slice, or start/end output range

key_params.name: cookpast
key_params.note: Cook skipped past values to avoid discontinuities

key_params.name: autoexportroot
key_params.note: Root path for automatic channel-name exports

key_params.name: exporttable
key_params.note: DAT table used by DAT table export methods

key_concepts: Object CHOP measures spatial relationships between a target object and a reference object.
The DAT Table can provide multiple target/reference object pairs, with target in the first column and reference in the second column.
Optional inputs can replace target and/or reference objects with XYZ point channels or standard Transform CHOP formats.
Compute can output transform formats, matrices, or measurements such as position, rotation, bearing, distance, and inverse-square distance.
Measurement output gives the target origin relative to the reference object's origin and rotation.
Channel naming can use plain channel names, target-prefixed names, or reference-prefixed names.
common_gotchas: The DAT table uses no headers; first column is target and second column is reference.
Point inputs must provide X, Y, and Z channels or a standard Transform CHOP format.
Objects and points can be compared with each other, but Rotation mode returns zero for points without orientation.
Rotation channels are selected to minimize frame-to-frame discontinuity, so values may be adjusted for graph continuity.
Cook Past Values can be slow because it may cook skipped frames to avoid discontinuities.
Use Object CHOP for spatial object relationships; Parameter CHOP and SOP to CHOP retrieve different object or SOP information.
